justifications.c1: Only rare catastrophic money figures (Powertrain compensation £500–£180k per claimant, £1m shared) and an HSE FFI rate of £166/hr; the routine cost of a drifted sump is small (disposal ~£0.20/litre, US $0.10–0.90/gal, half-hour labour) and the idea's £500–£2k per recharge is explicitly unconfirmed.
justifications.c2: HSE guidance requires weekly concentration, pH and bacteria checks per sump (HSE ebulletin search-confirmed, MW5, Scottish Engineering), and the 2023–24 HSE campaign found skipped fluid checks a common failing; a conductivity probe proxies only part of that weekly check (no bacteria).
justifications.c3: Documented weekly user checks and paid supplier fluid-management services (Fuchs, Oemeta on-site technician, QH FLUIDCARE, Millers), but no labour or contract cost found, and the manual tool is a <$20 refractometer.
justifications.c4: HSE COSHH essentials MW5 and HSE ebulletin set weekly checks; UKLA/HSE guide says check records retained 5 years; HSE's 2023–24 national campaign (press release search-confirmed) found failings at over half of sites with enforcement action, plus Powertrain improvement notices.
justifications.c5: No job advert or role description names the production or H&S manager as budget holder for coolant monitoring; budget is shown only indirectly via supplier fluid-care technician roles.
justifications.c6: MWF suppliers (Fuchs, Oemeta, Quaker Houghton, Master Fluids) and MRO distributors (MSC, Cromwell) already visit and sell fluid-management services including concentration/conductivity testing; no evidence they resell sensor monitoring.
justifications.c7: Comparable systems exist (FullShop Gen 3 subscription, search-confirmed but unpriced and North America only; Liquidtool; Okuma OEM) but no prices, customer counts or complaints; the UK per-sump gap is asserted from absence.
justifications.c8: Material sensing risk: conductivity is only a concentration proxy, refractometer errors of 30–40% are cited, and commercial systems draw samples to an external refractometer to avoid in-sump fouling (search also found FullShop's FAQ saying sump conditions foul inline sensors); no probe price searched.
justifications.c9: Weekly checks with 5-year record retention give a structural reason, and FullShop Gen 3 is sold as a subscription (search-confirmed), but no subscription price is evidenced.
justifications.c10: Three source types: regulator (HSE press release, HSENI campaign), trade press (British Safety Council, AM Online, Lubes'n'Greases), and first-hand forum posts (Practical Machinist, Hobby-Machinist, Dallas Makerspace), though forum posts are only loosely about skipped checks.

weakest: The money case: the routine cost of an out-of-spec sump is pennies per litre plus minutes of labour, and the only large figures come from a once-in-decades outbreak (Powertrain), so loss per site is unlikely to reach 5x product TCO.
